subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: MWCC GC 1.2.5. METHOD CORRECTION AND LANE-B RESULT for claim.law.inlined-callee-frames-reserve-dead-frame-bottom.20260831.v1. THE METHOD ERROR TO AVOID: that law's image census counts TARGET functions with a large untouched low region (216 with low_gap >= 32 image-wide) and both sweep work orders treat that as the candidate list. It is not one. A large target low_gap is not actionable by itself, because OUR build very often already reproduces it - the census must be run on BOTH the dtk-split target object AND our built object and reduced to the DELTA. Measured over the whole lane-B half (32 NonMatching units with path >= game/n excluding game/world/btricol, 495 functions carrying a frame): 74 functions have target low_gap >= 32, but only 19 have ANY nonzero target-minus-ours delta, and only 4 have |delta| >= 32. The target-only census over-nominates by roughly 4x. Concretely, the single cleanest specimen of the whole mechanism in lane B - sSetupWorldHeader in game/world/world.c, a zero-call big-endian header byte-swap with target low_gap 236, the exact shape the law's atree evidence describes - measures real 0 ALREADY: our source uses static inline sSwapU16/sSwapU32/sSwapF32 and reproduces the reservation exactly. It is a positive control for the law, not work. VALIDATION OF THE MEASUREMENT: the reusable recipe in the parent law (frame from `stwu r1,-N(r1)`; collect every N(r1) memory displacement plus every `addi rX,r1,N` and `mr rX,r1`; report min(referenced) - 8) reproduces that law's own published image-census numbers exactly on every lane-B entry it lists - ResolveWorldData 1252, InitWorldInfo 836, LoadPlyrData 776, InitEffects 356 - so the recipe is confirmed portable and the delta variant is a strict refinement of it. SIGN CONVENTION AND WHAT EACH SIGN MEANS: a POSITIVE delta (target reserves more than we do) means our source uses MACROS or open-coded shuffling where the original used inline helper FUNCTIONS - this is the productive direction and is what LoadPlyrData was (delta +152, closed to 0, real 1635 -> 465, see attempt.loadplyrdata-inline-frame-macro-conversion.20260831.v1). A NEGATIVE delta means we reserve more than the target, i.e. we inline where the original did not. CALIBRATION REFINEMENT: predicting the reservation as the plain 8-aligned sum of expansion frames UNDERSHOOTS. On LoadPlyrData the summed expansion frames were 764 (25 u16 helpers at 4 + 7 u32 helpers at 8 + 38 f32 helpers at 16) and the achieved, target-matching low_gap was 776 - a +12 residue exactly equal to the constant parameter-area-to-temps gap that claim.law.reserved-param-area-without-argument-stores.20260831.v1 independently measured (temps_base = 8 + P + 12). Predict low_gap = (sum of expansion frames) + 12 and treat the parent law's `8-aligned sum` as the lower bound. SCREENING RULE LEARNED: before nominating any delta candidate, check whether the function sits inside a `#pragma dont_inline` region - if it does, NO inlining occurs into it and the inline-frame mechanism cannot be the cause of its reservation, whatever its delta. This disposed of lane B's second-largest delta: game/ui/screensaver.c draw_inventory_panel (delta -56) is at line 884 inside that TU's dont_inline region spanning lines 834-1163, so the prior cap attempt.draw-inventory-panel-decl-reconstruction.20260831.v2 (recorded 06:38:54Z, i.e. 12.4 hours BEFORE the parent law, and therefore correctly re-opened for this screen under the park-age-vs-law-age rule) STANDS UNOVERTURNED, and its own conclusion - that the region is allocator spill reservation driven by register pressure - survives.
